text:
alex chen: Hey all — quick onboarding q. Trying to run streaming responses locally for a demo. Which key should I use: hosted or sandbox?
I can make non-streaming calls fine, but streaming continuously stalls behind our corp proxy. Also hit a couple of 429s while experimenting. Who do I ping for a small sandbox quota bump?

devon park: welcome! for local dev we usually tell folks to use the sandbox key. Hosted is for integration tests / staging. Sandbox has lower quotas but is safe for dev.

li zhao: fwiw streaming behind corp proxies can choke on chunked transfer. try curl with --no-buffer or in Node set highWaterMark, but the easiest is to run the request from your devbox without the proxy (if allowed) or via our dev-proxy which supports streaming.

alex chen: ah ok. where is the dev-proxy? I don’t see it in the onboarding doc. Do I need to whitelist an IP?

maria gonzalez: dev-proxy info is in internal tools -> dev-network. you can also use the hosted fallback if sandbox streaming is flaky, but watch quota. For IP whitelist, only for some legacy clients — your laptop shouldn't need it.

infra-bot: ACTION: sandbox-quota-request created (ticket #SAND-512). Tagging @platform-eng for quota review.

devon park: for the 429s, quick checklist: 1) confirm you're using the sandbox key (not rotated hosted key), 2) exponential backoff on 429, 3) if you hit sustained 429s open the ticket and include your thread + sample request.

alex chen: sample curl I'm running:
```\
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBOX_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-1","input":"hello","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
```
stalls after first chunk. any obvious mistakes?

li zhao: that looks fine. try adding `--no-buffer` (curl -N is same) + check corp proxy logs. If using Node, avoid libraries that buffer entire response (some fetch polyfills do). Also confirm you aren't behind a TLS-inspecting proxy that closes idle connections after N seconds.

maria gonzalez: regarding quota bumps — leave details in the ticket: your org, sandbox key prefix (last 6 of key), expected daily token volume. Platform eng will usually grant a dev bump same day.

alex chen: thanks! pinged the ticket with last6 and expected tokens. Last Q — for CI tests should we use sandbox or a hosted test key?

devon park: CI = hosted test key locked to CI project is preferred (so it’s isolated and has predictable quotas). Sandbox keys are intended for manual dev.

alex chen: perfect, appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

maria gonzalez: welcome aboard :partyparrot: if you want I can pair on one streaming test tomorrow morning.

alex chen: would love that, thanks!
